text:
alice: heads-up — the sample-stub helper in sample-app v0.9.2 is mangling tool/function-call JSON when an auth retry happens. saw this while onboarding a customer: the function payload arrives as a stringified JSON object instead of real JSON
ben: ugh, that sounds like the old double-encode issue. any logs/snippet?
alice: repro steps: 1) call sdk.tool.call('get_price', {...}) 2) auth token refresh triggers a retry 3) our retry wrapper re-encodes the body and then the json-mode helper calls JSON.stringify again. result: payload is '"{\"price\": 100}"' not {"price":100}
claire: can you paste the wrapper code? maybe the retry layer assumes body is a string already.
alice: here's minimal snippet:
```js
// inside helper.js
const body = prepareToolPayload(input); // returns object
await fetch(url, { body: JSON.stringify(body), ... })
// retry wrapper sees non-2xx and does: fetch(url, { body: JSON.stringify(body), ... }) again
```
ben: aha — prepareToolPayload sometimes returns a string for json-mode responses (to preserve whitespace). so JSON.stringify(string) produces a quoted string.
mark: short-term workaround: detect string payload and parse before re-stringifying. long-term: we need SDK parity between node+py: both should expose a single helper that takes a schema and an options bag (strict|coerce|preserveStrings).
claire: suggested helper API:
```js
// validateToolOutput(schema, { mode: 'coerce' | 'strict' | 'preserveStrings' })
await validateToolOutput(toolResultSchema, { mode: 'preserveStrings' })
```
ben: agree. also add an integration test that simulates token refresh mid-call (auth mock) and asserts that tool outputs remain typed objects, not double-encoded strings.
alice: temporary PR opened with naive fix (parse-if-string) — link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-app/pull/412 (please review) :eyes:
devex-bot: created issue #2543: "sdk: retry wrapper + json-mode helper double-encode causes toolcall payload to be string" assigned to @ben
mark: note for docs — call out that streaming + json-preserve options can return raw text pieces. make the sample-kit show how to set preserveStrings:false when you want structured outputs.
ben: i'll own the vendor PR to add parity tests for node & python. added to my todo. thanks for the clear repro, alice :thumbsup:
alice: thanks — customer unblocked with the workaround, but want the real fix in the SDK so sample apps don't bite new users during onboarding.
